papers.title: Computation-through-Dynamics Toolkit: Simulated datasets and quality metrics for dynamical models of neural activity
papers.reason: The paper provides simulated datasets and metrics for modelling biological neural dynamics, which is potentially useful for neuroscience modelling but is not specifically about planning, working memory, attention, or cognitive control.

papers.title: Erratum to "Selective Attention Deficits in Mild Traumatic Brain Injury using Steady-State Visual Evoked Potentials; Neural Correlates of Attention" [Clin. Neurophysiol. 192 (2026), 2112387].
papers.reason: The underlying topic is highly relevant to EEG correlates of selective attention in mild traumatic brain injury, but this record is only an erratum with no substantive findings provided.

papers.title: Metformin Preserves Regional Brain Glucose Uptake, Structure, and Functional Connectivity in Adults with Insulin Resistance.
papers.reason: The study links insulin resistance and metformin treatment to brain connectivity, prefrontal-dependent cognition, processing speed, and working memory in older adults, but its core focus is metabolic intervention rather than executive-function modelling.

papers.title: It is what it is: A comparative fMRI study on the regulation of negative emotions via distraction, reappraisal, and acceptance.
papers.reason: The paper reports fMRI evidence on prefrontal, cingulate, attention, and cognitive-control networks during emotion-regulation strategies, which could inform models of control but is not centred on classical executive-function tasks.

papers.title: Prefrontal activation predicts response latency and is shaped by age and lifestyle
papers.reason: The title suggests human neuroscience findings relating prefrontal activation to response latency, age, and lifestyle, but the absence of a summary makes the executive-function relevance uncertain.

papers.title: Characteristic Facial Expressions During Visual Fixation in Japanese Older Adults With Lower Cognitive Screening Performance: Exploratory Cross-Sectional Study
papers.reason: The study explores facial-video digital biomarkers for lower cognitive screening performance in older adults, but it does not specifically assess executive function or combine task behaviour with eye tracking or EEG.
